description: Every Saturday, our little mountain town in the Northwest Georgia mountains comes alive. Neighbors, families, and weekend travelers fill the streets as more than 1,000 people gather for what has become a true small-town tradition. People travel from all over Northwest Georgia, Southeast Tennessee, and beyond because they're searching for something that's becoming increasingly rare, a genuine farmers market. Here, you'll meet the farmer who grew your vegetables, the baker who made your bread before sunrise, the rancher who raised your beef, and the artisan who crafted your gift by hand. The LaFayette Farmers Market is more than a place to shop. It's where local farms, makers, and small businesses thrive, where families create Saturday morning traditions, and where community is built one conversation at a time.

description: We produce grass-fed beef and forest-raised pork while regenerating and restoring the land that we love using careful management. We employ intensive rotational grazing in our pastures, generally moving our cattle herd to a new paddock every day. Our cows are completely grass-fed from birth to finish. Our pigs are raised outdoors in a stress-free environment and forage for roots, nuts, insects, and plants on the forest floor. Their more varied diet, regular exercise, and exposure to sunlight result in more nutrient-dense meat that is much healthier for you, with a rich, delicious taste. Our management practices enable us to maximize plant recovery and soil health, sequester carbon from the atmosphere, maintain clean and healthy watersheds, and raise healthy, happy animals. Our sacred aim is to cultivate this land to the best of our ability and to produce meat that is healthy for our families and the families of our customers.

description: The Brookfield Farmers Market is a vibrant, community-driven event held on the west side of Brookfield Village Hall at 8820 Brookfield Avenue. Entering its 18th season in 2025, the market welcomes over 40,000 visitors annually, making it one of the most well-attended markets in the region. Open every Saturday from June through October, 8:00 AM to 1:00 PM, the market features a curated selection of local farmers, artisans, and small businesses offering fresh fruits and vegetables, baked goods, honey, sauces, handmade soaps, candles, and unique crafts. name: Kinnikinnick Farm - Feather Down Farm Days

description: We are a 5th generation farm using regenerative farming practices by integrating and bringing livestock back to the land. We raise Grass Fed & Finished Beef & Lamb, Mobile Pasture Raised Chicken & Eggs, and Timber Raised Pork. Our Chickens and Pigs receive homegrown Non-GMO feed. We treat our animals with respect and allow them to flourish in their natural environment and we are committed to their care. Our ruminant animals eat grass and cover crops for their entire lifetime. Any grains in our cover crop mix are grazed prior to grain formation. Chickens require grain and are fed organic grains along with fresh grass by moving their homes daily. Hormones, Pesticide, Vaccines and Wormer - none are ever given as they aren't needed with moves to fresh paddocks. Livestock have access to oilers filled with essential oils for fly and pest control. Our goal is to never administer antibiotics. Our customers never receive products that have been treated with an antibiotic.

description: Al-Munir Farms is a vibrant urban agritourism destination in Newark, NJ, operated by Al-Munir LLC. Our two primary sites—Eden’s Farm in the South Broad Street neighborhood and Jannah on Grafton in the North Ward—offer immersive, educational, and culturally relevant experiences centered around food justice, ecological sustainability, and community wellness. We host a wide range of public programs including farm tours, sustainable agriculture workshops, pollinator walks, community harvest events, and culturally affirming cooking demos. Our work is rooted in Black, Indigenous, and Afro-diasporic traditions, and features ethnobotanical crops from Africa, the Caribbean, Latin America, North America, and the Indian Subcontinent. As a SARE-funded research site and participant in the USDA’s EQIP and SNAP-Ed programs, Al-Munir Farms also serves as a model for regenerative agriculture and community-led research. We welcome school groups, families, and civic organizations to visit us.

name: Ghost Light Farm
description: Ghost Light Farm is home to our herd of Commercial and Registered Black Angus cattle. We breed, calve, wean, and finish on our 170-acre property. The herd roams freely on pasture, drinks from spring fed ponds, and grazes together on grass in the summer. In the winter we provide hay and balage from our fields and purchase some additional forage from our neighbors. Our finishers also eat a ration of corn we purchase from a nearby farm and whiskey-mash from a local craft distillery. We sell our beef direct-to-consumer at on farm, at farmer's markets, and through a monthly subscription. We also sell beef and value-added products to restaurants, whole animal butcher shops and independent grocery stores. We work exclusively with a USDA inspected processing facility that is Animal Welfare Institute approved.

name: McComb Farmers Market
description: The McComb Farmers Market is more than a place to shop, it's a place where community grows. Each market brings together local farmers, bakers, artisans, and small businesses while creating a welcoming space for neighbors, families, and visitors to connect. Every purchase supports local entrepreneurs, strengthens our local economy, and helps preserve the small-town spirit that makes McComb special. What truly sets our market apart is the experience. From live music and food trucks to our signature Sprouts Kids Club, every market offers something for all ages. Through hands-on activities, children learn about agriculture, nutrition, entrepreneurship, and healthy living while earning Sprout Bucks to spend with vendors, creating a fun and meaningful connection between kids and local businesses. The McComb Farmers Market isn't just about fresh food, it's about building relationships, supporting one another, and creating traditions that bring our community together.
directions: The McComb Farmers Market is located in Town Square at 131 E. Main Street, McComb, OH 45858, in the heart of downtown McComb. The market is held in the parking lot between 129 E. Turn left onto Main Street (OH-235), continue into downtown, and you'll find the market on your left. From Lima (35 minutes): Take State Route 65 North to State Route 613 West into McComb. Continue to Main Street, and the market will be in the Town Square. From Bowling Green (35 minutes): Take I-75 South to Exit 159 (State Route 613). Head west on OH-613 into McComb and continue to downtown Main Street. From Fostoria (25 minutes): Take State Route 23 South to State Route 613 West. Follow OH-613 into McComb until you reach the Town Square on Main Street. Free parking is available on surrounding downtown streets and nearby public lots.

description: Cuyahoga Valley Farmers Markets’ (CVFM) works to provide access to and education about sustainable foods and agriculture to the communities in Northeast Ohio by building connections between our community with the producers of locally grown food. CVFM was established in 2022 to continue the operation of the long-running Countryside farmers markets in Howe Meadow and at Old Trail School, both located in the Cuyahoga Valley National Park. These vibrant farmers markets have been in operation since 2004 and have been growing steadily since their inception. CVFM MARKET IMPACT: During our Summer market in Howe Meadow (May-October) we connect on average 2,500 (peak 3,000) members of our community to producers of local food. description: Weavers Way Farm Market offers local organic seasonal produce as well as local dairy, freshly baked bread, local ice cream, pasture-raised eggs and meats, raw honey, flowers, and more! Produce grown at Weavers Way Farms is sold at The Farm Market. The Farm Market is located at Saul Agricultural High School. The farm and market operate in collaboration with the high school and provide educational opportunities for Saul students, who manage the farm along with their teachers and Weavers Way staff. Like the Co-op stores, the market is open to the public — you don’t need to be a member of the Co-op to shop. Weavers Way Co-op member benefits also apply at the market, including working member discounts, Food for All (low-income) discounts, and senior discounts. As payment, we accept cash, credit/debit/EBT cards, EasyPay (for Co-op members), Farmers Market Nutrition vouchers (FMNP), Philly Food Bucks and Food Bucks Rx. Visit our website for hours at weaversway.coop.
directions: Parking options: Upon entering the parking next to the Farm Market (watch for Farm Market signs), you can park at the first parking lot to the right, or in the grass in front of the pasture to the left of the livestock barn. description: The West Allis Farmers Market, located at 6501 W. National Ave., is open from the first Saturday in May through the Saturday after Thanksgiving. It is open on Tuesdays and Thursdays from 12 p.m. to 5 p.m. and on Saturdays from 1 p.m. to 5 p.m. We open later in the day to allow the farmers to bring only the freshest produce, picked that morning, to the market. The Market welcomes only Wisconsin-based growers and makers, so you can shop local and enjoy the best Wisconsin has to offer. The West Allis Farmers Market is an open-air, European style market that has been operating since 1919.
